title: Kernel-checked enclosures of DESI DR2 BAO distances in Lean 4: certifying solver output with integer certificates
description:
A small end-to-end example of certified numerics for cosmology. For the flat ΛCDM best fit to the DESI DR2 BAO data (Ωm = 0.29743, radiation off), Lean 4 theorems checked by the kernel, using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and without native_decide, enclose the dimensionless comoving distance χ(z) = ∫0z dz'/E(z') at all seven DESI DR2 effective redshifts with relative width 2.5–2.8 × 10-4.

Method: 1/E is decreasing, so Riemann sums on a grid bound the integral; an untrusted program supplies integer bounds of 1/E at 4661 grid nodes and the kernel re-checks them by exact integer arithmetic (decide +kernel); a soundness theorem proved in Lean/Mathlib lifts the check to the integral.

The certified enclosures were used to audit a Rust CVODE reimplementation (rusty-SUNDIALS) and astropy: their values lie inside, a deliberately loose CVODE run (rtol = atol = 10-2) falls outside at 3 of 7 redshifts, and the enclosures at Ωm × 1.01 are disjoint from the fit's. Hypotheses and controls (Einstein–de Sitter closed form, tampered table rejected by the kernel, planted sorry/axiom flagged) were preregistered. The paper also gives research directions from a survey of the openai/math Lean library against this programme, which contributes certificate methodology rather than physics results.

Not claimed: the fit point is a rounded floating-point fit, not certified as the χ2 minimum; D_V/r_d, the conversion to D_M/r_d and D_H/r_d, and the comparison with DESI are computed outside Lean from the certified bounds; no new physical result. Work carried out with the assistance of an AI model (Claude, Anthropic) under the author's direction.
notes: Preprint v1. Pilot P1 of a certified-numerics programme; companion to doi:10.5281/zenodo.23245266.
